6.0.0.en: The principles of the doctrine of Christ: the fundamentals of the Christian life.

6.0.2.en: Not laying again: not occupied with.

6.0.3.en: Dead works: the sins that deserve death.

6.0.4.en: Baptisms: he means the sacrament of Baptism with the details of its prayers and its kinds for infants or adults.

6.0.5.en: Laying on of hands: the laying on of the hands of the Apostles and bishops to give the Holy Spirit after Baptism (that is, the sacrament of the Holy Myron). The Apostle Paul calls the believers to leave the talk about the fundamentals of the Christian life in order to advance in spiritual growth, and these fundamentals are:

6.0.6.en: 1- Repentance and faith, which represent the basis of man's readiness to enter Christianity.

6.0.7.en: 2- Baptism and the Holy Myron, which are the first two sacraments that God gives to those coming to Christianity.

6.0.8.en: 3- The resurrection and judgment, which are the hope of those who have begun the Christian life, that is, the resurrection of their bodies on the last day and passing the last judgment to enter the Kingdom.

6.0.9.en: All these fundamentals he has finished speaking about, and they need to be occupied with spiritual growth. This is what the Apostle indicates is the most important and will do, that is, he will speak about how to grow spiritually in order to enjoy fellowship with God.

6.1.0.en: Once enlightened: they received the sacrament of Baptism.

6.1.1.en: The heavenly gift: the sacrament of the Holy Myron, that is, the descent of the Holy Spirit.

6.1.2.en: The powers of the world to come: they performed miracles and experienced God in their lives with deep spiritual feelings, which are a glimmer of the light of eternity.

6.1.3.en: Fall away: apostatize from the Christian faith.

6.1.4.en: To renew them: it is not possible to repeat their baptism if they repent and return to the faith.

6.1.5.en: They crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame: the baptized person dies with Christ by being buried in the water of Baptism and then rises with Him, so the one who is baptized receives the power of Christ's crucifixion, death and resurrection, and this happens once, and Christ cannot be crucified twice for the baptized man, so if Baptism were repeated it would be as though we crucify Christ another time and put Him to shame, that is, clothe Him with disgrace after He rose from the dead.

6.1.6.en: In these verses the Apostle Paul answers a question concerning those who have apostatized from the faith, after receiving the sacrament of Baptism and the Myron and the gifts of the Holy Spirit and enjoying the word of God and even performing miracles and experiencing the work of God in them: is their baptism to be repeated? He says that their baptism cannot be repeated because renewal means Baptism and not repentance in the sacrament of confession, and renewal happens once because it is a death and resurrection with Christ, who died and rose once, so this happens in man once and he receives a new nature; and if it is soiled by sin, even if it be apostasy from the faith, it is healed by repentance and confession. This view is the view of St. John Chrysostom.

6.1.7.en: And there are views of other Fathers such as Tertullian, which is that these verses mean the Jews who became Christians and then returned to their Jewish life and insist on not returning to Christianity, or everyone who insists on his sins and does not want to repent and return to Christ; they interpret the word fall away as meaning persistence and continuance in sin throughout life, and accordingly their not being renewed and receiving forgiveness in the sacrament of confession is due to their own refusal and not God's rejection of them, and by their sins they crucify Christ a second time and clothe Him with disgrace and shame by their refusal to repent.

6.2.0.en: He likens the spiritual man who is steadfast in the faith to land on which rain falls, that is, God's blessings through spiritual teachings and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, so it yields good plants, that is, fruits of the Holy Spirit which the believers enjoy and God rejoices in them and gives them the glories of the Kingdom.

6.3.0.en: He completes the comparison and says that if this land does not produce good fruits after receiving abundant rains, meaning those who believed and lived with Christ for a time and then apostatized and fell into various sins, they are rejected by God and near to destruction, and the solution is their repentance and return to the faith from which they apostatized, so that God forgives them and they regain their membership in the Church.

6.3.1.en: May you benefit from God's continual blessings to you which you receive from the Church in the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace, and not take them superficially so that their work in you is lost; and the sacrament of repentance restores your spiritual zeal so that you become active anew and deepen your relationship with God.

6.4.0.en: The Apostle qualifies his words and encourages the Christians of Jewish origin with his confidence that they enjoy the Christian life and the blessings of salvation in the Church, and that by his previous words he meant a warning against apostasy from Christ, and if one of them falls, his repentance can be accepted in the sacrament of confession. He is concerned to encourage them so that they do not fall into faintheartedness or despair because of their weaknesses.

6.5.0.en: For God is not unrighteous to forget the good works and their sincere love which they showed in labors for the sake of His name, to Him be glory, since they did not stop serving the believers and continue in that to this time.

6.6.0.en: Some Christians showed their concern for serving those in need, so Paul wishes that all the believers would care about these services, and he encourages them to continue and care about good works throughout their lives, for they are the proof of their faith and their hope in God.

6.7.0.en: He continues to encourage them to reject laziness and to imitate the holy fathers, such as Abraham, in holding fast to the faith, patience in hardships and continuing the striving until they obtain God's promises and inherit the Kingdom.

6.7.1.en: Take care to encourage others, for it is in most cases more acceptable and effective with people than reproach and rebuke. Rebuke and punishment are important at times, but because of suffering from many afflictions, which sometimes lead to negligence and laziness, people need to regain their confidence in themselves and in God's love through your kind words. And this encouragement gives you too zeal and hope.

6.8.0.en: God wanted to confirm His promise to Abraham with an oath as people are accustomed to confirm their words, and since He found no one greater than Himself to swear by, He swore by Himself to confirm the truth of what He promises.

6.9.0.en: God promised Abraham many blessings and descendants too many to be counted.

6.10.0.en: Abraham believed and was patient in enduring sufferings and lived a righteous life, so he obtained God's promises when Isaac was born while he was a hundred years old and Sarah ninety, and this was a prelude to God's blessings which Abraham would receive in heaven.

6.11.0.en: For it is the custom of people, when affirming facts to their hearers in case of any dispute between them, to swear by the greatest they know in order to confirm their agreement and covenants. And God permitted swearing by His name in the Old Testament to declare that He is the one God and not the gods of the pagan Gentiles, but in the New Testament He forbade it because there was no need for it after faith in Him had become established.

6.12.0.en: Therefore when God wanted to confirm His promise to Abraham and to his children, who are we the believers, He used an oath.

6.13.0.en: In order that God might gladden us and establish our hope in Him, He confirmed the truth of His word by two things, which are:

6.14.0.en: An anchor: the anchor that is cast into the sea to fix in its bottom and hold the ship so that the waves do not carry it away from the shore, and it is a symbol of the hope that establishes the spiritual man in life with God. The veil: the curtain that separates between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies and which only the high priest passes through, once every year, with blood to make atonement with it before the ark of the covenant that is in the Holy of Holies. And passing through the veil signifies Christ's passing through and His ascension into the heavens as High Priest to intercede for us and prepare a place for us there.

6.14.1.en: The Apostle likens hope to an anchor that establishes the spiritual man in the love of eternity, which Christ prepared for us and passed into as our representative by His ascension after His resurrection, and He remains there interceding for us forever because He is a priest after the order of Melchisedec, that is, the eternal priesthood, and not the temporary, symbolic priesthood of Aaron in which bloody sacrifices are used.

6.14.2.en: Look to the hope of eternal life and God's promises to you so that you are encouraged however afflictions surround you, for they are temporary, and trust in the love of God, who turns afflictions into blessings and gives you in place of them glories in heaven.

7.0.s.en: (1) The priesthood of Melchisedec is greater than the priesthood of Aaron

7.0.0.en: For this Melchisedec, the great one, king of Jerusalem, whose name was formerly Salem, that is, peace or king of peace, was in the days of the first fathers a priest of the Most High God; this priest and king met our father Abraham, the father of fathers and greatly honored among the Hebrews, when he was returning victorious over the four kings who took Lot captive, and the Old Testament mentions that this Melchisedec blessed the father of fathers Abraham (Gen 14).

7.1.0.en: Abraham felt the greatness of Melchisedec, so he gave him a tenth of the spoils he obtained from his victory over the four kings, and the giving of the tithe was a sign of his priesthood, and Abraham asked for the blessing from Melchisedec. The meaning of the name Melchisedec in the Arabic language is king of righteousness, and also king of Salem in the Hebrew language: that is, king of peace.

7.2.0.en: This Melchisedec appeared suddenly in the Divine inspiration without any mention of who his father or mother was or his lineage in order to prove the validity of his priesthood, since in the Aaronic priesthood it was necessary to be sure of the validity of a person's descent from Aaron so as to be accepted as a Jewish priest (Ezra 2:62). And the Old Testament did not mention the beginning of Melchisedec's life or its end because he is likened to our Lord Jesus Christ, who has no father in the flesh and has neither beginning nor end, for He is eternal and everlasting, and because our Lord Jesus Christ is the Son of God He remains a priest forever.

7.3.0.en: Consider, O Hebrew brethren, how great this Melchisedec was, for our father Abraham, the chief of the first fathers, the one of the divine calling, from whom came the whole Hebrew people, gave him a tenth of the spoils he had, which is a sign of Abraham's submission to Melchisedec by asking the blessing from him.

7.4.0.en: While Abraham gave tithes to Melchisedec like this, without any command mentioned beforehand concerning Melchisedec, we find that the priests of the tribe of Levi, who have the right of the priesthood in the Old Testament in Israel, take tithes from their brethren, with less honor, by a commandment of the Law, and not as Abraham gave Melchisedec tithes of his own accord as a sign of submission and a request for blessing.

7.4.1.en: And we notice that all the tribes give tithes to the tribe of Levi although these tribes have the honor of Abraham because they are his descendants, but the commandment orders them to give tithes to the tribe of Levi, which like them is from the descendants of Abraham. So it appears from this that the honor of the tribe of Levi is less than the honor of Melchisedec, although both take tithes.

7.5.0.en: Melchisedec, whose lineage is not known, blessed Abraham, who received the promises from God, and took tithes from him, and from him came the tribe of Levi, which takes tithes from its brethren, that is, the rest of the tribes.

7.6.0.en: Without all contradiction: certainly and without dispute.

7.6.1.en: There is no doubt that he who gives the blessing is greater than he who receives the blessing, that is, Melchisedec was more honored than Abraham.

7.7.0.en: Mortal: their lives end in death.

7.7.1.en: The priests of the tribe of Levi who take tithes end their lives in death, but Christ the High Priest lives forever in the likeness of Melchisedec, who took the tenth from Abraham, because Melchisedec is a type of Christ; Christ is living, whereas the Levitical priesthood is merely a symbol of Him because the priests of the Old Testament die.

7.8.0.en: So that I say to you a word that settles the comparison between the Levitical priesthood, to which some of you may try to hold fast, and the priesthood of the Lord Christ, which is after the order of the priesthood of Melchisedec: that Levi, who took tithes from the people in the person of Aaron the priest, paid tithes to Melchisedec, a sign of honor, because he was still in the loins of his father Abraham, who represents the whole Hebrew people, since from his descendants, that is, from the descendants of Abraham, all the tribes of the people came forth, including the tribe of Levi.

7.8.1.en: If you are humble you can receive God's blessings from many people and see their virtues and learn from them, and since God sees your humility He gives you many graces beyond what you ask, so learn from everyone, even children.

7.9.s.en: (2) Perfection in the priesthood of Christ

7.9.0.en: If the perfection of salvation was through the Levitical priesthood, when the people of the children of Israel received at its hands the Mosaic Law and the legislation of the Old Testament, why did the psalms prophesy of the coming of another priest after the order of Melchisedec and not after the order of Levi, that is, the priesthood of Aaron: “The LORD sware, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek” (Ps 110:4).

7.10.0.en: Since the priesthood has among its tasks conveying the message of the Law from God to the people, the mention in the psalm of the change of the priesthood from the tribe of Levi to the priesthood of Melchisedec is a decisive proof of the need to change the Law needed for the salvation that God wants to teach the people, so that it changes from the Law that was given at the hand of the Levitical priesthood, a law that gave perfection to no one, to the law of the grace of Christ Jesus, who came after the order of Melchisedec, fulfilling the prophecy that came about Him in (Ps 110:4).

7.11.0.en: He of whom these things are spoken: he means Christ.

7.11.1.en: Because the One spoken of in this prophecy, our Lord Jesus Christ, was of a tribe from which no one served as priest or attended at the altar, for it is known to everyone that our Lord Jesus Christ came from the tribe of Judah, of which Moses gave no commandment to perform the priestly work.

7.12.0.en: Confirming that the Law must be changed, the psalm made clear that another priest in the likeness of Melchisedec would come afterward, and he is Christ.

7.13.0.en: The priesthood of the Lord Christ, which is after the order of this Melchisedec, was not for us to give us an external, fleshly commandment that does not affect our souls or change them, but it is a priesthood that gave us the power of righteousness and the grace of inner change and an everlasting life that does not pass away.

7.14.0.en: The psalm (Ps 110:4) testifies that the Lord Christ will be a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec, that is, as Melchisedec offered in his priesthood an offering of bread and wine and did not offer an animal sacrifice, so also the Lord Christ offered a bodily sacrifice under the appearance (form) of bread and wine (Mt 26:26-27).

7.15.0.en: By Christ the usefulness of the Law was ended and the shortcoming of what the Levitical priesthood offered appeared, for it gave us only an external commandment that exposes sin but does not give power to be rid of it, and a commandment that urges to righteousness but without giving us the ability to practice it.

7.16.0.en: Because the Law did not complete our salvation, we necessarily needed another salvation, and this was accomplished by Christ, who gives us hope, a hope by which we can draw near to God, unlike the people in the Old Testament, who had to stand far off, unable to approach God or the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.

7.16.1.en: Do not reject any new idea because you have become accustomed to another thought, but examine it with care, for it may be the more correct, and prayer with the guidance of guides supports you to know what is better.

7.17.s.en: (3) The reasons for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ

7.17.0.en: The first reason for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ is that God confirmed it with an oath, but those priests of the Levitical order became priests without a word of oath, because they were merely a type of the One typified, the Lord Christ, to Him be glory, the true Priest, the One of whom God assured us with an oath in the Divine inspiration in the psalm, saying that God swore and will not at all go back on His word that you (Christ) shall remain a priest forever after the order of Melchisedec (Ps 110:4).

7.18.0.en: By the greatness of the divine oath Christ became as a representative of mankind and a priest for ourselves who guarantees us a new and better covenant with its spiritual promises and the work of God's rich grace in our lives.

7.19.0.en: The second reason for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ is the weakness of the priests of the Old Testament, because they are men who die, so there were accordingly many of them, one to take the place of another.

7.20.0.en: But our Lord Jesus Christ, because He is God manifest in the flesh and living forever, is distinguished and different from the human, mortal priests of the tribe of Levi in His remaining forever, and as a result His priesthood does not pass away or end, because the person of Christ, to Him be glory, does not die.

7.21.0.en: That come unto God by him: they take shelter in His blood that atones for them.

7.21.1.en: On this account, and because of the remaining of Christ, to Him be glory, living forever, He is able to save to the uttermost, that is, even after our death and our standing before God in eternal life; we also find Him supporting us after our death, interceding for us before the Father as a priest who feels our weaknesses, and we take shelter in Him before the fearful and just God; this is because He lives at all times above the ages.

7.21.2.en: And here we notice that the priestly ministry of the Aaronic high priest stops at his death, whereas our Lord Jesus Christ began by His death, as a sacrifice for the sins of the world, His priestly ministry, which lasts forever.

7.22.0.en: The third reason for the greatness of the priesthood of Christ is His holiness and His innocence of every sin; He who, as proof of His righteousness, has been lifted above sharing in the deeds of our sinful world, glorified with great honor, and was able to enter the Holy of Holies of heaven without offering a sacrifice for Himself like the high priests of the Levitical priesthood, who are always compelled, in making atonement for the sins of the people, to offer several sacrifices and not one sacrifice; they offer sacrifices first for themselves because they are sinners like the rest of the people for whom they offer the sacrifices. But Christ does not need a sacrifice because He is without sin, but He offered Himself as an atoning sacrifice for the whole world once, because in His redeeming work is the perfection of salvation, so it does not need to be repeated by Him.

7.23.0.en: For the Law of the Old Testament set up for us men weak people as high priests only in symbol, who cannot offer us complete salvation, but the word of God in His oath, which was made clear to us in the psalm that came after the Law, revealed to us the person of our Lord Jesus Christ, the true Priest, who completed for us and for our sake this eternal salvation. And this is proof of the insufficiency of what came in the Law for our salvation, we men.

7.23.1.en: If Christ has offered us a great salvation like this, let us hold fast to Him by our attachment to the Church and distance from every sin, and as much as we thank Him, we live in His righteousness, caring about every good work. Christ gives us heaven and the blessings of the New Testament. St. Paul continues in this chapter to draw a comparison between the earthly Hebrew high priest from the tribe of Levi and the Lord Christ, and here he brings out the distinction of the Lord Christ, to Him be glory, for in His priestly work He is able to enter the Holy of Holies of heaven itself, not the Holy of Holies of an earthly tabernacle made by men as a model which God gave to man of the true, heavenly tabernacle in which God dwells.
